title: Sedentary Blocks
user: Desk workers with Apple Health or exported wearable data who need to see the few long uninterrupted sitting periods worth changing, rather than another step total.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The asker has a watch that records steps but cannot find an iPhone app that totals daily inactivity/sedentary minutes.
A separate tracker user requests automatic messages for people exceeding a configured inactivity time.

recurrence: Two independent tracking contexts in 2025 ask for inactivity-time visibility/action; the pain is daily and current activity rings do not expose the long-block pattern.
current_workaround: Infer it from step/stand totals, set generic watch reminders, or inspect raw health charts.
incumbents_and_gap: Apple Health and Fitbit emphasize activity totals; Stand reminders are interruption-based. Neither makes an exported-data, private daily map of long sedentary blocks and user-defined exceptions the main artifact.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA that imports Apple Health XML/CSV, lets a user mark sleep and travel windows, and renders a printable day/week timeline of sitting blocks with a simple break target. Non-goals: medical advice, live watch notifications, social challenges, or cloud sync.
success_measure: In a 14-day pilot, 50% of users identify and shorten at least one recurring sedentary block by 15 minutes without enabling more than one reminder.
monetization: one-time — an import-and-review utility has durable personal value without requiring health-data hosting.
constraints: All parsing stays in-browser; clearly state estimates depend on source granularity; no diagnosis or health claims; support deletion by clearing local data.
why_distinct: It is a privacy-preserving interpretation of inactive time, not a step tracker or a nagging break-reminder clone.

title: Mood Context Calendar
user: People who already jot down a daily mood and need a low-pressure way to notice their own context patterns without outsourcing intimate journal data.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An HN user explicitly asks whether people keep a mood journal, why they started, and whether it has helped.
The requested calendar combines planned training with mood captured on each day, demonstrating demand for a time-based contextual view.

recurrence: Two independent 2025–26 requests converge on recording mood and viewing it beside life activity; the challenge is sustaining reflection without clinical overclaiming.
current_workaround: Use a notes app, a mood app with streaks, or a paper diary, then mentally reconstruct what was happening that day.
incumbents_and_gap: Daylio, Apple Journal, and generic diaries capture entries, but often prioritize streaks, feeds, or cloud backup rather than a user-owned calendar that links only a few chosen personal context tags.
smallest_useful_product: Offline calendar with one mood check-in, optional free-text note, and up to five user-created context tags (sleep, work, exercise, travel). It shows only user-authored correlations and exports JSON/printable pages. Non-goals: AI analysis, diagnosis, social sharing, or therapy replacement.
success_measure: At least 40% of first-week users make 10 entries and can name one personally useful context pattern in a follow-up survey.
monetization: one-time — sensitive journaling should remain functional without a subscription or account.
constraints: Local encryption option and explicit export/delete controls; no medical or mental-health treatment claims; accessibility for color-independent mood display.
why_distinct: The value is a deliberately small, user-controlled context calendar, not an AI therapist or gamified mood tracker.

title: Health Visit Packet
user: Patients preparing for an appointment who need a compact, accurate packet of their own labs, medicines, questions, and observations from scattered portals.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A practicing physician asks people living with wearables, patient portals, labs, and notes about the pain of health data scattered across sources.
An offline emergency-health-card feature requires continuous offline fallback testing, underscoring the need for health information that remains available without a service.

recurrence: A clinician's discovery request and an independent offline-health project both expose the same ownership and availability problem; appointment preparation is episodic but high-stakes.
current_workaround: Open several portals during the visit, carry screenshots, or manually assemble a document in Notes/Word.
incumbents_and_gap: Patient portals, Apple Health, and personal health-record apps store pieces of the record. They do not reliably produce a user-curated, source-labeled, offline visit packet without asking the user to centralize records in another cloud.
smallest_useful_product: Browser-only packet builder: paste/import selected values, attach source/date, add questions and a medication list, then generate a printable PDF and encrypted local bundle. Non-goals: OCR automation, record scraping, clinical interpretation, provider messaging, or emergency decision support.
success_measure: In interviews, 8 of 10 users can create a first packet in under 15 minutes and report that it replaced at least two portal/login lookups at their next visit.
monetization: one-time — users should not pay an ongoing fee merely to access a document they assembled.
constraints: No health advice or diagnosis; data must stay on device by default; PDF export needs a visible data-minimization warning and no analytics.
why_distinct: It is a preparation and handoff artifact, not a universal health-data platform.

title: Medication Handoff Card
user: Adult children and caregivers coordinating an older relative's medication list who need to record changes and hand a clear, dated list to family and clinicians.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The asker says an elderly family member loses track of many medicines and a shared Google Doc fails to keep family and doctors updated.
An OpenMed request seeks to preserve the family-member relationship for conditions, showing that family context is routinely lost in health records.

recurrence: Two 2026 health-data requests show family context and current medication facts becoming detached; errors are potentially severe even though this product must not provide medical advice.
current_workaround: Shared documents, a paper list, pill organizers, or an app that only the patient controls.
incumbents_and_gap: Apple Health Medications, Medisafe, and pill dispensers handle reminders or an individual list. The gap is a printable/change-focused handoff record that shows who confirmed each item and what changed, without creating a caregiver surveillance service.
smallest_useful_product: Local-first medication list with dose/timing/free-text prescriber fields, change log, owner/last-confirmed line, and large-type print/PDF card. Non-goals: drug-interaction checks, dosage recommendations, dispensing, refill ordering, alerts, or cloud accounts.
success_measure: A caregiver can produce a dated, one-page list with a change history in under five minutes and at least 70% of pilot users update it after a medication change.
monetization: one-time — the core value is a durable personal record, not recurring medication engagement.
constraints: Prominent non-clinical disclaimer; no interaction database; local encrypted export option; account for accessibility and print legibility.
why_distinct: It improves human handoffs and accountability around a list, rather than becoming a medication-adherence or telehealth platform.

title: Private Statement Review
user: Privacy-conscious households who download bank CSVs and need a quick monthly review of cash flow and recurring charges without connecting an account to a financial-data intermediary.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The asker rejects bank links and cloud uploads, finding spreadsheets too manual and self-hosted finance tools too complex.
A P0 report describes an unauthenticated CDN exposing users' financial files, a concrete reason users resist hosted financial-document storage.

recurrence: A direct consumer request and a 2026 security incident both reinforce privacy as a hard requirement, not a cosmetic preference; setup complexity is the adoption blocker.
current_workaround: Spreadsheets, an infrequent manual statement review, or a Docker-heavy budgeting installation.
incumbents_and_gap: YNAB, Monarch, Actual Budget, and Firefly III are capable. The unresolved space is a no-account, no-bank-link monthly review that starts with a downloaded statement and does not demand full budgeting discipline.
smallest_useful_product: Offline CSV importer with a remembered local mapping, merchant merge/split rules, recurring-charge candidates, month comparison, and exportable review checklist. Non-goals: bank aggregation, investment advice, credit scoring, automatic categorization by cloud AI, or multi-user sync.
success_measure: At least 60% of pilot users complete two monthly CSV reviews, with no transaction data leaving the browser, and identify one unexpected recurring charge or category change.
monetization: one-time — privacy credibility and low setup cost matter more than an ongoing consumer-finance subscription.
constraints: Never transmit statements; redact values from diagnostics; preserve source CSV locally only on opt-in; no financial advice or institution credential handling.
why_distinct: It is a lightweight statement-review ritual for people avoiding aggregation, not another full budgeting system.

title: Family Handoff Calendar
user: Two-parent households juggling school, work, pickups, and activities who need to see who is responsible at each handoff without committing their family schedule to Google or Apple.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A parent asks for a shared family calendar that is movable and self-hostable rather than bound to Google or Apple.
A family-calendar project scopes profiles, shared calendar data, preferences, multi-device sync, and an optional self-hosted backend.

recurrence: Independent 2025–26 family-calendar requests show ecosystem lock-in and coordination are persistent; the specific daily failure is an unowned pickup or handoff, not calendar rendering.
current_workaround: Shared Google/Apple calendars, group chat, a wall calendar, or generic task apps.
incumbents_and_gap: Cozi, TimeTree, Google Calendar, and self-hosted CalDAV cover events. They make responsibility secondary; a household needs a fast 'who has the child/item next?' handoff view that can work from an imported ICS file.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA importing/exporting ICS, with named household members, handoff/pickup tags, a next-48-hours responsibility board, and a printable week sheet. Non-goals: messaging, location tracking, school integrations, accounts, or automatic calendar hosting.
success_measure: In a four-week pilot, households record 80% of scheduled handoffs and report zero missed handoffs caused by unclear ownership.
monetization: one-time — a family organizer should keep working without a subscription or account lock-in.
constraints: Calendar data remains local; careful timezone/ICS handling; do not collect children’s data or offer tracking; shared-device export must be explicit.
why_distinct: It layers responsibility and handoffs on top of portable calendar files instead of replacing calendar infrastructure.

title: Home Project Ledger
user: New homeowners running several repairs or improvements who need one local decision record linking quotes, scope changes, spent-to-date, and the documents that justify them.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A new home-maintenance membership advertises simplification beyond one-off call-outs, indicating continuing homeowner demand for maintenance coordination.
A home-improvement tracker request explicitly requires projects from ideas through planning, budgeting, completion, timeline, and maintenance concerns.

recurrence: A market entrant and a separate household-tool request identify planning and ongoing maintenance as one homeowner workflow; lost decisions and quotes turn into real money/time waste.
current_workaround: A folder of PDFs/photos, notes, spreadsheets, contractor email, and separate task lists.
incumbents_and_gap: Trello, Notion, Houzz, and contractor CRMs are broad or service-centric. The gap is a homeowner-owned ledger that makes the decision, quote, receipt, and future-maintenance implication reviewable together.
smallest_useful_product: Local web app with per-project scope, option/decision log, quote comparison, spend lines, attachment references, and an exportable closeout sheet. Non-goals: contractor marketplace, payments, permitting advice, collaboration SaaS, or price estimates.
success_measure: At least half of pilot homeowners attach or link all documents for one active project and can answer spent-vs-approved in under one minute.
monetization: one-time — value is concentrated around a home’s projects and users should retain their records indefinitely.
constraints: Attachments stay in browser storage or as file references; no contractor endorsements; currency/tax fields must not imply legal or financial advice.
why_distinct: The primary artifact is an auditable homeowner decision ledger, not a generic project board or lead-generation marketplace.

title: Home Maintenance Receipts
user: Households that need to remember recurring upkeep and prove what was done, when, and with which documents when selling, insuring, or simply troubleshooting a home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN user seeks a family-friendly way to organize and share documents, notes, and to-do lists rather than scattered services.
A home-maintenance-report request specifically calls for PDF export and inclusion of permit documents.

recurrence: The family organization request and dedicated maintenance-report request converge on evidence, not merely reminders; the consequence is lost household history when it is needed.
current_workaround: Calendar reminders plus email search, paper binders, photo albums, and a generic drive folder.
incumbents_and_gap: HomeZada, Centriq, and maintenance memberships can track homes but often center cloud inventories or vendor services. A narrow local record of completed work and its documents is underserved.
smallest_useful_product: Offline log of appliance/system, completed task, date, provider, cost optional, next-due date, and attachment hash/link; generate a one-page-per-system PDF report. Non-goals: contractor booking, automated diagnosis, insurance claims filing, or smart-home control.
success_measure: Pilot users can locate a maintenance date and supporting receipt in under 30 seconds for 90% of logged items after three months.
monetization: one-time — durable home records should outlive a subscription and work while offline.
constraints: No external storage by default; make backup/export prominent; never claim a log satisfies warranty, permit, or insurance requirements.
why_distinct: It treats completed-work evidence and portable reports as the product, rather than a broad home inventory or reminder app.

title: Meal Plan Pantry Check
user: People who keep a personal recipe list and want a deterministic shopping list that subtracts only what they personally confirm is in the pantry.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A user built a personal flow from selected recipes to a consolidated shopping list, then checks what is already in the cupboard.
A Mealie bug report on quantity management shows that ingredient quantities remain a concrete failure point in meal-planning workflows.

recurrence: A personal tool builder and an active meal-planning issue both point to the same fragile join: selected recipes, quantities, and what is already at home.
current_workaround: Copy ingredients into Notes, use an LLM-generated list, or maintain a heavyweight recipe server and manually resolve quantities.
incumbents_and_gap: Paprika, Mealie, AnyList, and Recipe Keeper offer recipe and list features. The lightweight gap is a local, explainable list that shows every source recipe and requires explicit pantry confirmation rather than pretending inventory is exact.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA where users paste a few structured recipes or ingredient lines, select servings, normalize simple units, tick pantry items, and export a grouped checklist with source links. Non-goals: URL scraping arms race, nutrition advice, grocery ordering, barcode inventory, or AI recipe generation.
success_measure: At least 70% of pilot meal plans produce a list in under five minutes, and users report fewer than two forgotten ingredients per four planned meals.
monetization: one-time — a small household tool should work without grocery-affiliate incentives or data collection.
constraints: Ingredient parsing must expose uncertainties; units are not nutrition/medical measurements; do not scrape protected recipe content or retain URLs remotely.
why_distinct: It is an explainable pantry-confirmed list builder, not a recipe-content app or a thin prompt around meal planning.

title: Garden Rotation Cards
user: Home gardeners with a handful of beds who need a simple record of what grew where and a transparent warning before repeating a crop family too soon.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A plant-app builder includes care reminders and health reports among the features users expect once they start tracking their plants.
A garden-planner request calls for recording N-way soil rotation events and showing provenance-aware warnings.

recurrence: A 2025 consumer plant-tracking launch and a 2026 planning request point beyond identification toward ongoing garden memory; seasonal recurrences make forgotten bed history likely.
current_workaround: Paper garden maps, photos, spreadsheets, seed packets, or generic plant-care apps.
incumbents_and_gap: Gardenize, GrowVeg, and plant-identification apps cover journals, designs, or identification. The missing small utility is a transparent, offline bed-history card that explains its warning from the user’s own record.
smallest_useful_product: Static/offline web app for named beds, crop-family tags, planting/clearing dates, simple notes, and printable rotation cards with 'last occupants' rationale. Non-goals: AI identification, weather prediction, pest diagnosis, seed sales, or agricultural recommendations.
success_measure: By the second planning session, 60% of pilot gardeners enter all active beds and can verify a proposed crop against last season’s family in under 20 seconds.
monetization: one-time — personal garden history is seasonal and should remain accessible year after year.
constraints: Clearly frame warnings as user-configurable planning prompts, not agronomic advice; no location collection; provide CSV/print backup.
why_distinct: It preserves provenance for a very small garden-rotation decision rather than competing with plant-ID or full garden-design tools.

title: Training Log Merge
user: Recreational athletes mixing gym plans with running or wearable workouts who need one private weekly training view without forcing all activity into a single app.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The asker observes several friend groups using workout accountability chats and monthly leaderboards, showing recurring need to see and sustain training activity.
A Wger user says manual running tracking is not comparable to gym exercise data and requests connection to apps such as Strava.

recurrence: Social accountability and a separate gym-versus-running logging request show split training records in 2026; the practical pain is comparing the week, not getting an AI coach.
current_workaround: Switch among Strava, a strength app, a watch dashboard, spreadsheets, and chat-based accountability.
incumbents_and_gap: Strava, Strong, Hevy, Garmin Connect, and Wger each own a modality. They do not offer a local import-only weekly training ledger that preserves source links and lets a user decide how different sessions count.
smallest_useful_product: Offline importer for simple CSV/GPX workout exports plus manual strength sessions; display a weekly timeline and user-set session labels/load notes, with CSV export. Non-goals: coaching, leaderboards, heart-rate interpretation, live device sync, or social network.
success_measure: At least 60% of pilots import two sources and complete a weekly review for three consecutive weeks without duplicating a session.
monetization: one-time — source-neutral personal history is more trustworthy when it has no engagement or social-data business model.
constraints: Do not make performance or health claims; local-only processing; source adapters must respect export formats and trademarks; clear time-zone handling.
why_distinct: It reconciles a user’s existing training exports instead of trying to replace a workout logger or build an AI fitness agent.

title: Health Export Cleaner
user: Wearable users who want to keep, move, or share a bounded slice of their own health data while removing precise location, identifiers, and fields they did not intend to disclose.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The asker wants an open-source, community-driven way to export/import/transfer personal data and explicitly includes fitness apps among hard-to-move services.
A fitness project requires enforcement that health data is not used for advertising or cloud backup, making non-retention a concrete product constraint.

recurrence: A broad portability request and a 2026 privacy requirement converge on user control of fitness data; sharing a sample currently risks oversharing the entire export.
current_workaround: Send the full Apple Health/fitness export, manually edit CSVs, or give another app account-level access.
incumbents_and_gap: Apple Health export, Google Takeout, vendor downloads, and generic CSV editors provide raw files. They do not make it easy to create a documented, minimized subset with precise fields and date range chosen locally.
smallest_useful_product: Browser-only tool that reads a supported health CSV/XML export, selects date range and record types, drops identifiers/GPS/routes, bins timestamps, previews row counts, and writes a provenance note with the cleaned file. Non-goals: health analysis, cloud transfer, vendor scraping, EHR integration, or de-identification guarantees.
success_measure: In usability tests, 8 of 10 users produce a desired minimized sample in under 10 minutes and correctly identify which fields were removed before download.
monetization: free — transparency and interoperability are strongest as an inspectable local utility; paid support can follow only if needed.
constraints: Never claim anonymization; process only locally; defend XML/CSV parser against large and malformed files; document residual re-identification risk and source-format limits.
why_distinct: It is a data-minimization and portability tool, not another health dashboard or data broker.
